headline: sisu opens the trail with 194.02; Warthogs fall by 0.56
lede: First week of the season and the territory's already sorted itself into 8 teams struttin' and 8 teams checkin' their wagon wheels. sisu came out of the canyon firing and put 194.02 on the board, while e-mans revenge limped home with 65.25 and a bad taste. And down at the far end of camp, Jack Attack beat Warthogs by 0.56, which is thinner than the shave I got in town.
paragraphs: sisu hitched Derrick Henry to the front of the wagon for 36.35 and rolled clean over densmen, 194.02 to 145.56, the widest margin of the week at 48.46. densmen weren't sleepwalkin' either: Jalen Hurts went for 24.16 and Ventrell Miller turned in the best defensive day in the league at 14.5. Trouble is densmen left Jalen Coker and his 27.1 sittin' on the bench, and Coker happens to lead all 104 qualifying men in the whole country at +12.7 pts per game over expected, efficient or lucky, take your pick. Brandon Aubrey kickin' in 1.0 didn't help the cause any.

Jrod rode Caleb Williams for 38.43 and handled Aeil, 142.18 to 113.28. Aeil got 25.0 out of the Seahawks defense, which is a fine thing, but Myles Garrett posted a flat 0.0 and Malik Willis sat on the bench with 16.15 in his pocket. Jrod's own ledger ain't spotless: Colston Loveland put up 0.0 and a better lineup was worth 16.35 more. Won anyway, and the winners buy the coffee.

Zihuatanejo won the ugliest footrace in camp, 87.23 to 65.25 over e-mans revenge, and still managed the worst lineup of the week. A better arrangement would've added 33.55, with T.J. Watt and his 21.0 watchin' from the porch. Lamar Jackson did the honest work at 28.08. For e-mans revenge, D'Andre Swift's 29.70 was near half the team's whole haul, the Texans defense turned in 0.0, and 65.25 is the low mark of the entire league this week.

Super Troopers took it 121.8 to 101.53 over Scott's Hype, with Brock Purdy steady at 25.75. Jaylen Waddle managed 0.5, which is close enough to nothin' to hurt, and it still didn't matter. Scott's Hype leaned on the Vikings defense for 16.0 and got 1.65 from Quentin Johnston, and left T.J. Hockenson's 9.4 on the bench. Super Troopers only left 5.2 on the table, tidiest housekeepin' in town.

Long Howie edged Justin's Bad Team 102.02 to 86.66 behind Justin Jefferson's 22.8. Justin's Bad Team actually had the best man on the field, Kenneth Walker at 32.35, and got 0.0 out of Kyle Pitts Sr. to go with it. Deebo Samuel Sr. and his 11.6 sat out the whole affair, and a better lineup there was worth 14.25. Rashid Shaheed's 0.6 says Long Howie had some rough ground of its own.

Norskes U Betcha survived WeBleedOrangeAndBlue by 9.77, 127.1 to 117.33, with Trevor Lawrence throwin' for 28.65. Both outfits left silver in the creek: Tyler Shough scored 35.2 on the Norskes bench and Bryce Young scored 35.52 on the other. WeBleedOrangeAndBlue got 32.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and would've added 30.19 with a better lineup, which is a mighty uncomfortable number when you lose by 9.77. Jordan Addison's 0.0 didn't hold Norskes back, and that's luck you don't get twice.

Dart Vader did the thing the team name promised, 30.5 from Jaxson Dart, and took HAWKSRULE 98.75 to 89.35. HAWKSRULE topped out at Dak Prescott's 17.0, watched De'Zhaun Stribling post 0.0, and left Fred Warner's 11.0 on the bench for 18.1 in missed lineup. Dart Vader had Baker Mayfield and his 16.02 idlin' too. Nine and a bit points is a short rope, but a win's a win.

Closest race of the week and the meanest: Jack Attack 103.53, Warthogs 102.97, decided by 0.56. Josh Allen hung 40.23 on the board for Jack Attack, which was near enough to cover Romeo Doubs' 0.0 and the 23.0 the Chiefs defense scored while benched, 30.25 worth of better lineup left in the dirt. Warthogs got 20.0 from Javonte Williams, 1.35 from Courtland Sutton, and sat Jordan Love with 21.14. Two teams left a fortune in the creek and one of 'em still had to walk home.
sign_off: 12 weeks left in the regular season and 8 seats at the playoff table, pardners. Plenty of trail to ruin yourself on.
purse: The commissioner's strongbox opens for 4 this week: sisu takes 1st with 194.02 for $40, densmen 2nd with 145.56 for $20, Jrod 3rd with 142.18 for $10, and Norskes U Betcha 4th with 127.1 for $5. First trip to the pay window for every one of 'em, and it spends just the same come season's end.
